paragraphs: Gloucestershire County Council runs its own fostering service, Fostering Gloucestershire, and the independent agencies shown above also approve carers here. When a child in the council's care needs a foster home it looks to its own carers first and asks agencies when it has none free. Enquiries to the council now come through the South West Fostering Hub, which takes first calls for 15 councils in the region.

The council's sufficiency strategy for 2025 to 2028 says it had around 800 children in its care in September 2024. Fostering is how most of them are looked after, at 68%, and of the children living with foster carers about seven in ten are with the council's own carers and three in ten with agency carers. The council wants more children to grow up in the county, close to home: it records that around a quarter of those placed outside Gloucestershire live more than 20 miles away, and it aims for a net gain of ten foster places a year and to grow its Mockingbird groups, in which an experienced hub carer supports a cluster of nearby families, from two to one in each district.

The strategy names teenagers, children with complex physical, emotional or behavioural needs, and unaccompanied young people as the main pressures. The council's vacancies page says it most needs long-term homes for children over five, carers who can keep brothers and sisters together, homes for over-tens and teenagers, short breaks of at least two weekends a month for children over 10, and carers for disabled children.

To apply to the council you need to be over 21 with a spare room, have experience of caring for children (your own children must be over two), hold a driving licence and have basic IT skills. You can be single, married, divorced or living together for at least two years. Council carers have a supervising social worker who visits at least every eight weeks, training and development workshops, support groups and consultations with a child therapist in their first year. We do not yet have a Gloucestershire allowance page, so ask the council and each agency for its current fees and allowances.

Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before you decide. The Gloucester page covers the city itself, and the South Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Worcestershire, Herefordshire and Oxfordshire pages list services nearby.
